tips.title: Choosing the Right Glue for Different Plastics
tips.text: For polystyrene (PS) parts common in most kits, use Tamiya Extra Thin Cement (Item 87001). For ABS parts found in some modern kits, use Tamiya Cement (Item 87003) in the green bottle. For soft or delicate PE parts, use CA (Cyanoacrylate) glue like Loctite Super Glue Ultra. Apply sparingly, press parts together immediately, and let cure for recommended time before handling.

tips.title: Selecting the Right Paint Type
tips.text: For most applications, use Vallejo Model Air or Model Color acrylics. They're water-based, easy to clean, and provide excellent adhesion. For metallic or clear finishes, consider Vallejo Metal Color or Alclad II. For enamel effects, use AMMO by Mig Jimenez enamels. Always thin paints with their respective brands' thinner for best results.

tips.title: Choosing the Right Sandpaper Grits
tips.text: For initial surface preparation, use 150-220 grit sandpaper to remove mold lines and flash. For smoothing putty or filler, use 220-320 grit. For final sanding before painting, use 400-600 grit. Always wet-sand to minimize dust and swirl marks. Use sanding sticks or blocks for even pressure.

tips.title: Selecting the Right Filler for Gaps
tips.text: For small gaps and seams, use Tamiya Putty (Item 87126). For larger gaps or porous surfaces, mix Vallejo Plastic Putty with water until it reaches a creamy consistency. Apply with a brush or spatula, let dry, sand smooth, and touch up with paint. Alternatively, fill gaps with CA glue and baking soda for a rapid, abrasive filler.

tips.title: Choosing the Right Decal Setting Solutions
tips.text: For most cases, use Microscale Micro Set (Item 71.260) to soften and Micro Sol (Item 71.261) to slide decals into place. For thicker or more fragile decals, use Mr. Mark Softer (Item 73002) for gentle setting without dissolving the decal paper. Always follow up with Micro Sol to ensure full adhesion.
